body_markdown:
# Introduction

The last sound of an English word can change its meaning. If you leave it out, listeners may misunderstand the word. Practise word endings clearly without adding an extra vowel.

## 1. Final P, T and K

These sounds are made by briefly stopping airflow.

- cap
- sit
- book
- stop
- work
- help

Say the final sound clearly. Avoid adding an extra “uh” after it.

## 2. Final B, D and G

These are voiced consonants.

- cab
- bad
- bag
- job
- need
- dog

Compare:
- cap / cab
- bet / bed
- back / bag

The final sound changes the word.

## 3. Final F and V

- leaf / leave
- safe / save
- belief / believe

For F, use air without voice. For V, use the same general mouth position with voice.

## 4. Final S and Z

- rice / rise
- bus / buzz
- face / phase

Listen for the difference between the unvoiced and voiced final sounds.

## 5. Practise in short sentences

- I need a new bag.
- Please stop here.
- The dog is outside.
- I will save the file.
- The bus is late.

## Common mistakes

- Dropping the final consonant.
- Adding an extra vowel after the final sound.
- Confusing voiced and unvoiced pairs.
- Speaking so quickly that the ending becomes unclear.

## Practice

Choose the word that completes each sentence.

1. Please close the (cap / cab) of the bottle. Choose the word meaning a cover.
2. I need a new (bag / back) for school.
3. I will (save / safe) this document.
4. The (bus / buzz) is waiting outside.
5. I have a lot of (work / worked) to do. Choose the base noun.

**Answers:** 1. cap, 2. bag, 3. save, 4. bus, 5. work.

## Speaking practice

Read the word pairs cap/cab, bet/bed, back/bag and leaf/leave. Record yourself and check whether the final sound is audible.

## Learning tip

Give special attention to the last sound of a word. A clear ending often matters more than speaking quickly.

faq.question: How can I practise this pronunciation lesson?
faq.answer: Listen to the examples, repeat them aloud, practise in short sentences and record your voice.

faq.question: Should I copy one particular English accent?
faq.answer: No. Focus on clear, consistent pronunciation that listeners can understand.

faq.question: How often should I practise?
faq.answer: A short daily session of 10 to 15 minutes is a useful routine.
